extraction.name: TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents
extraction.description: TravelPlanner is a new planning benchmark that focuses on travel planning, a common real-world planning scenario. It provides a rich sandbox environment, various tools for accessing nearly four million data records, and 1,225 meticulously curated planning intents and reference plans.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark construction pipeline involves environment and evaluation setup, diverse travel query design, reference plan annotation, and quality check. Queries are constructed by randomly choosing departure city, destination, and date range, then adjusting duration and number of hard constraints. Human annotators meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Data is sourced from publicly available Internet data: FlightSearch from Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset, DistanceMatrix from Google Distance Matrix API, RestaurantSearch from Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset, AttractionSearch from Google Places API, AccommodationSearch from Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset. Data is modified to suit requirements.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Flight data spans from 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01. Other data collection timeframe not specified.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Original data is modified by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to suit requirements. For FlightSearch, price is generated by multiplying distance by a random factor. For DistanceMatrix, price is calculated by multiplying distance by factors. For RestaurantSearch, restaurants are randomly assigned to cities and categorized under cuisines. For AccommodationSearch, items are randomly assigned to cities and given random room rules.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data is stored in a static database to ensure consistency. Agents are instructed to use the 'NotebookWrite' tool to record necessary information for planning to prevent maximum token limit.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 20 graduate students are invited to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries. One plan is deemed eligible only if it meets all constraints outlined in the evaluation script. Annotators are paid an average of $0.80 per plan.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Authors performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found. Budgets are re-calibrated using costs from human-annotated plans. Multiple stages of human verification ensure high quality.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4-Turbo is used for key components extraction from natural language plans.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: TravelPlanner aims to provide an effective benchmark for complex planning in future research. Data is derived from publicly available data and does not represent authors' viewpoints. Evaluation criteria are based on authors' consensus, with encouragement for additional discussions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The static sandbox environment ensures consistent and unbiased evaluations by avoiding variability from dynamic data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Current evaluation criteria for commonsense are based on authors' consensus and may not capture all perspectives. The benchmark is challenging; even advanced agents achieve low success rates.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, Testing. The training set includes 45 queries with human-annotated plans, validation set includes 180 queries, test set includes 1,000 queries. Usage guidelines prohibit cheating in validation and test sets.
